decisions.reason: A cube top face may be subdivided at x=1/2 into two coplanar faces while its mesh triangles cross that line. Set lambda=1 on the left subface and zero on all other faces. Every facewise gradient vanishes, but a crossing triangle has a nonconstant restriction, hence nonzero mean-projection error. A smooth bump inside one side of that triangle detects the error in the H^(-1/2) dual. The claimed gradient-only bound and step 1.2 therefore fail: this is a logic defect, not a missing citation.

reviews.reason: Checked the chart/Fourier conventions, convex Poincare supplier and zero-mean duality. Retained the family-independent H^(1/2)-to-L2 estimate and clarified H1 regularity of its smoothed restrictions across coplanar seams. Added the general h^(1/2) negative-norm residual bound for every L2 density. The h^(3/2) gradient bound now covers every elementwise H1 density, including facewise C1 densities on face-fitted meshes, with no continuity required across mesh edges. No new supplier or choice assumption is needed. This is the repairer’s verification, not independent review.
